newsitem.title: USA: Polaroid launches digital microscope camera.
newsitem.headline: Polaroid launches digital microscope camera.

text.p: Polaroid Corp will begin shipping next week the Polaroid Digital Microscope Camera (DMC), designed specifically for microscopy applications, officials said Thursday.

The camera, which retails for $5,995 in the U.S., offers high resolution at a lower price and is the first camera specifically designed for microscopy applications, Jim Landrigan, senior manager of medical and scientific imaging with Polaroid said at an industry presentation.
"By targetting this particular price point, the DMC is really applicable for a wide-variety of applications," Landrigan said.
The DMC can be used for semiconductor, pharmaceutical, biotechnology and material science and other industry applications, he said.

Polaroid will next week begin shipping the DMC in the U.S. to a narrow spectrum of full-service microscope dealers and to the same distribution points in Europe and Asia in mid-September, he said. "We're not looking for broad distribution of this product," Landrigan said.
The DMC allows users to capture 24-bit color images at resolutions of 1600 x 1200 pixels as well as 800 x 600 pixels.
The DMC compliments Polaroid's other offerings for the microscope camera market, including instant film and film scanners, he said.

Landrigan declined to estimate the size of the potential market for the camera but said of the approximately 190,000 microscopes sold in the U.S. each year, perhaps 40 percent may be candidates for the camera.
"The transition from film to digital has not been as fast a transition as we would have thought," Landrigan said.
